turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Mrs Rao, please come. I will just check the pressure before you go in.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes sister, thank you. We were waiting outside only from quarter to 10, the token queue was moving slow, but we are here now.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): BP is 108 over 68. Pulse 86. Oxygen 99 percent.
[SEG0004] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sorry, parking was too much. I am Vikram, her husband.
[SEG0005] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sit. How many weeks?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Twelve weeks and 3 days. LMP was the 14th of March, and both my phone app and the gynaecologist in Koramangala gave the same date, so the dates are not in doubt.
[SEG0007] person_4 (DOCTOR): Why today?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): I want my blood tested, doctor. I need to know if I carry it too, for the baby's sake. I have been turning it over in my mind every single night.
[SEG0009] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): At a camp in Jayanagar last month they said I have thalassaemia trait. HbA2 was 5.2 percent on that paper. I got very tensed for her.
[SEG0010] person_4 (DOCTOR): Right. Any long-standing illness?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, asthma, since my college days. It is the mild type, I have never been admitted, touch wood, and I manage it with the inhalers only.
[SEG0012] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any operation before?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): No, never. Not even a tooth extraction, nothing like that.
[SEG0014] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any bleeding?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Not even spotting. I check every morning because I read too many articles, but there has been nothing at all.
[SEG0016] person_4 (DOCTOR): Tummy pain?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Not really. There is a stretching low down sometimes, like a small pull, but it is not pain.
[SEG0018] person_4 (DOCTOR): Vomiting?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I had vomiting in the first month, mostly mornings, but it has gone completely, and I am eating rice and sambar normally now.
[SEG0020] person_4 (DOCTOR): Fever? Cough?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Never. No fever, no cough.
[SEG0022] person_4 (DOCTOR): Breathless on walking?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Not that either. I climb two floors to the flat and I am alright.
[SEG0024] person_4 (DOCTOR): Wheeze at night?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): No... well, sometimes. Two or three nights in a week I wake up a little tight in the chest, and it settles if I sit up.
[SEG0026] person_4 (DOCTOR): Smoke? Alcohol?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Never smoke, never alcohol. I take only one small coffee in the morning, and even that I am thinking of cutting down.
[SEG0028] person_4 (DOCTOR): Mm. Medicines?

[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Folic acid 5 mg, one tablet every morning, started when we began planning the pregnancy. The brown inhaler, budecort, two puffs morning and night. Asthalin only when I need it, one or two puffs.
[SEG0030] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Doctor, she misses the night puffs sometimes. I have seen that inhaler not used.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm, yes, some nights I forget if I sleep early. Also they gave me ferous sulphate, one tablet a day, but I stopped it in March because my stomach was not agreeing.
[SEG0032] person_4 (DOCTOR): You took the iron, or never started?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): I took it for about ten days, then I stopped it in March. They also spoke of a deworming tablet, but I never took that one.
[SEG0034] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any drug reaction?

[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, penicilin. At 19, for a throat infection, within one hour I got hives all over and my lips swelled. They told me never to take penicilin again, so I have avoided it completely.
[SEG0036] person_4 (DOCTOR): Chest. Lungs are clear, no wheeze just now. Tummy is soft.

[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Is that alright? I was frightened the night tightness means the asthma is worsening in pregnancy, because I read it can change, and my mother-in-law has been saying all sorts of things.
[SEG0038] person_4 (DOCTOR): Asthma is stable enough. Today is carrier screening. Nothing is confirmed about the baby.
[SEG0039] person_4 (DOCTOR): I am booking a blood count, HPLC for thalassaemia, and a ferritin, today.
[SEG0040] person_1 (NURSE): I will take her to the lab after this. I can print the forms now.
[SEG0041] person_4 (DOCTOR): If the HPLC shows you also carry the trait, we might do a detailed scan, and we might send you both for genetic counselling. Not otherwise.

[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): And if I am negative, doctor? I need it clear in my head, because he is a carrier, so is the baby still at risk of the major disease or only when both of us carry it? I keep circling on this.
[SEG0043] person_4 (DOCTOR): If you are negative, the baby cannot have thalassaemia major. Let's see in two weeks with the reports.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Should I restart the iron on my own? I will continue the inhalers, I will not stop those, and I always tell doctors about the penicilin.
[SEG0045] person_4 (DOCTOR): Do not restart the iron yourself. Continue the folic acid and both inhalers. No penicillin-group medicines. Bring the camp report if you have it.
[SEG0046] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I have it in the file. I can give a xerox.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): Err, one more thing. My sleep is very broken from the worry, I am up till 1 or 2 thinking about the baby. Do we treat that?
[SEG0048] person_4 (DOCTOR): Not with a tablet today. See me in two weeks. The nurse will finish the bloods.

spec.situation: Couple, wife pregnant, husband found to carry thalassaemia trait at a camp; both anxious; blood tests for the wife planned; genetic counselling discussed.

traps.happens: The doctor asks about drug reactions. Variants (use ONE per encounter): (a) the patient says 'No, never, I have taken penicillin and everything' (no allergy); (b) the patient is unsure ('maybe the antibiotic or the painkiller, nobody told me which'); (c) a real allergy with the reaction described; (d) allergies are never asked.
traps.label_rule: (a) NO allergy entry: negative_findings 'Allergies' absent. (b) allergy with status uncertain, the substance as described, the reaction if said, plus an allergy_uncertain uncertainty. (c) allergy with the reaction. (d) nothing at all. NEVER list a medicine the patient has taken without a reaction as an allergy, and the plan must not prescribe a drug of a recorded allergy's family.

traps.happens: The patient denies some symptoms (said as 'no', 'not really', 'never'), has a chronic condition named earlier (for example asthma or hypertension) and later the doctor asks about another symptom of it, and one answer is a double negative or a correction ('not that either', 'no... well, sometimes').
traps.label_rule: Denials go in negative_findings with the exact thing denied, never in symptoms. NEVER write a negative about a condition the patient has said they have. A corrected answer keeps only the final version. A negative is never a symptom, and 'not painful' is the finding 'pain' absent, not a symptom called 'painless'.

features: hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.

stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.

bad.reason: Stretching low down sometimes is reported, but category musculoskeletal is not stated.
bad.text: Lower abdominal stretching (category=musculoskeletal, status=present, frequency=sometimes, temporality=current, body_site=lower abdomen, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

bad.reason: She says not really pain, but mentions stretching/pull; absolute absence of abdominal symptoms is overstated.

bad.text: Blood count (type=laboratory, status=planned, requested_by=doctor, indication=thalassaemia carrier screening in pregnancy)

bad.reason: Ferritin is planned, but indication 'iron stopped in pregnancy' is inferred, not stated.
bad.text: Ferritin (type=laboratory, status=planned, requested_by=doctor, indication=iron stopped in pregnancy)
